newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy recovering at a gradual pace - EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy recovering at a gradual pace - EPA.

text.p: The gradual recovery in Japan's economy has not been derailed despite some weakness in business sentiment, as economic fundamentals continue to show slow but steady improvement, the government said on Friday.
"Economic fundamentals are generally improving, but business sentiment is still cautious, so our overall assessment remains unchanged," an Economic Planning Agency (EPA) official told reporters.

In a regular report on the health of the economy, the government's economic policy research unit said the recovery was making only slow progress and that it still needed the help of easy credit to reach a self-sustaining stage.
The report also prescribed remedies for the economy such as deregulation and expansion of domestic demand, but stopped short of mentioning any additional fiscal stimulus measures.
"The economy is continuing to recover, as seen in the increasingly bullish tone in private-sector demand, but the tempo of the recovery is gradual for now," the EPA report said.
The latest monthly economic report was virtually unchanged in its core evaluation, using the same phraseology as before.
The government declared in February that the nation's economy had finally come out of the slump that followed the collapse of the late 1980s "bubble" economy.
But the EPA has not been able to take its assessment further than a "gradual recovery" since then.
"We have not been able to confirm that the current recovery has become a self-sustaining one," the official said.

Although overall business sentiment continues to brighten, some companies have become cautious, as can be seen in sluggish growth in industrial output, the high level of inventories and the still worrisome unemployment rate, the EPA official said.
The official said the government weakened its assessment of business sentiment after looking at the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) quarterly "tankan" corporate survey, unveiled late last month.

The tankan showed that the business outlook among major manufacturers had worsened, with the diffusion index for major manufacturers falling to minus seven in August from minus three in the previous survey in May.

But exports have grown as the weakness of the yen against the dollar in the past year has helped Japan-made products, especially cars, regain their competitiveness in overseas markets, the EPA official said.
He also noted that the jobless rate, though still at a high level, had come down to 3.4 percent in July after posting a record 3.5 percent for the previous three months.
Asked whether the government had strengthened its economic assessment at all, the EPA official said: "I'd say it has moved just a bit forward."
An increase in corporate capital spending was confirmed by the BOJ's tankan survey and private consumption is recovering as well, helped by a better labour environment, he said.
"The tempo is gradual, but we are heading towards self-sustainable recovery," he said.
But worrisome factors remain, such as a falling off of public works spending later this year and the effect of a planned rise in the consumption tax on housing investments.
The current sluggishness in the semiconductor market may also force companies to revise down their capital spending plans later this year, the EPA official said.
